dedupe_keys.name: reducing computational complexity of neural networks in optical channel equalization from concepts to implementation

description: Costa, Nelson and colleagues document this resource in the B5G-OPEN community. The implemented methodology compresses feed-forward and recurrent coherent-optical equalizers using quantisation, weight clustering and pruning. Bayesian optimisation selects compression hyperparameters while balancing performance and complexity. Coverage includes simulated and experimental optical transmission and four reported complexity metrics: RMpS, BoP, NABS and NLGs. The study compares against digital back-propagation and chromatic-dispersion compensation. Hardware synthesis in a separate companion resource is a distinct implementation step; shared experimental independence is not asserted. Zenodo provides the descriptive publication with open access; its stated licence is cc-by-4.0. Its publication licence does not establish a code licence or source-code availability. A limitation is that the native metadata do not establish all implementation settings, uncertainty bounds or independent reproducibility. Only descriptive metadata were inspected. Related records and companion papers retain their source-defined roles; they do not imply independent measurements.
